report.scope: US market, whey concentrate and isolate powders for everyday use. Plant powders appear only as a caution. Prices seen Nov 10–13, 2026.

primer.what_it_is: Powdered milk protein you mix into water, milk or smoothies to hit a daily protein target, most often for training or weight management.

must_haves.why: Enough to count as a real serving of protein.
Shows the protein is mostly whey, not cheap fillers.
Checks the protein claim and heavy metals, since there are no federal limits.

premium_features.why: Less lactose and fat; worth it if dairy upsets you.
A sourcing preference; it doesn't add protein.

premium_features.feature: Sport certification (NSF Certified for Sport, Informed Choice)

avoid.why: Mostly sugar; one popular gainer was flagged for arsenic.

avoid.thing: Comparing by price per tub or per serving
avoid.why: Scoop sizes differ; compare price per gram of protein.
Consumer Reports found high lead in almost all plant powders it tested.

verdict.headline: Kirkland whey at about 3¢ per gram is the value floor; most people don't need isolate.
verdict.confidence: Moderate: five prices seen this week; others come from price trackers and reviews.
verdict.reasoning: Per gram of protein, Kirkland ($0.030) and sale-priced Myprotein ($0.026–0.03) cost about half of Gold Standard at Walmart ($0.047). Isolates run 5.4–8.5¢ and boutique grass-fed 8–12¢, paying for lactose removal and labels rather than more protein.
verdict.price_watch_summary: Kirkland 5.4 lb is $56.74 on Costco same-day; warehouses range $48.99–$64.99. Buy at $57 or less.

recommendation.product: Kirkland Signature Whey Protein, Creamy Chocolate, 5.4 lb
recommendation.why: The lowest price per gram of protein seen, and Costco rarely discounts it further.

normalization.unit_rationale: Price per tub or per serving misleads: tubs range from 400 g to 2,100 g of protein, and scoops from 20 g to 28 g. Price per gram of protein is the only fair comparison.
normalization.quality_adjustment: Grams of protein = servings × protein per scoop from the label. Treat isolate as a digestive upgrade, not more protein. Mass gainers and blends count only their protein grams.
normalization.formula: Price per gram = tub price ÷ (servings × grams of protein per scoop)

bands.label: Value isolate
bands.verdict: Pay this only if you need isolate

normalization.size_economics: Bigger tubs are cheaper per gram: Gold Standard is about 3.7¢ in Costco's 5.64 lb tub vs. 4.7¢ in Walmart's 5 lb. Small 20–30 serving bags carry the highest per-gram prices.

diminishing_returns.knee_example: Kirkland Signature Whey, 5.4 lb, at $56.74 (about 3¢ per gram)
diminishing_returns.below_knee: Below ~2.6¢ per gram there's little left to save; going lower usually means gainers or blends with less real protein.
diminishing_returns.above_knee: Above ~4.5¢ per gram you pay for isolate filtering, flavors, grass-fed sourcing or certification, not more protein.

value_traps.instead: Whey plus real food for calories.

value_traps.instead: Whey, or a plant powder with published heavy-metal tests.

consensus.expert_view: Value rankings put Kirkland and sale-priced Myprotein at the top per gram; Consumer Reports found whey generally lowest in lead and recommends checking for third-party testing.
consensus.community_view: Lifters favor Kirkland and Gold Standard for value and taste, buy isolate only for digestion, and treat boutique brands as optional.
consensus.where_they_disagree: Reviewers often rank premium isolates highest for taste and purity; value-focused rankings favor concentrates.

price_segments.why: Concentrate, isolate or boutique grass-fed sets the per-gram price more than brand does. Tub prices cover 400–2,100 g of protein, so compare the per-gram range.

segments.label: Concentrate / blend
segments.what_you_get: Ordinary whey (about 70–80% protein); fine for nearly everyone who digests dairy.
segments.best_pick: Kirkland Signature Whey Protein, Creamy Chocolate, 5.4 lb
segments.watch_out: Blends with milk protein or added amino acids can inflate the label.

segments.label: Isolate
segments.what_you_get: Filtered further to ~90% protein with little lactose: easier on sensitive stomachs, mixes thinner.
segments.best_pick: NOW Sports Whey Protein Isolate, unflavored, 5 lb
segments.watch_out: Costs about 2x concentrate per gram; skip it if dairy doesn't bother you.
